description.narrative: The goal of this proposed NAP Readiness Project is to establish a resilient and inclusive national adaptation planning ecosystem in Mozambique, enabling transformational, long-term shifts towards climate resilience. This framework will integrate climate adaptation into national, regional, and sectoral development planning, strengthen institutional capacities and mobilize sustainable financing for prioritized climate actionsTo combat pressing climate challenges, Mozambique has formulated a series of strategic policies that prioritize resilience and adaptation across vulnerable sectors.. Together, these policies establish a comprehensive approach to enhance Mozambique’s adaptive capacity and align with international climate commitments:1. National Strategy for Adaptation and Mitigation of Climate Change (ENAMMC), 2013-2025: 2. National Adaptation Plan (NAP): 3. Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)In analyzing Mozambique’s adaptation framework key barriers that hinder cohesive, scalable climate change adaptation and resilience efforts:1. Limited governance and institutional coordination2. Deficient planning processes and technical capacity: effective climate adaptation requires robust planning processes, which Mozambique currently lacks, especially at the sub-national level. 3. Limited and inconsistent climate data:Mozambique faces data discrepancies between ministries, gaps in historical climate data and limited capacity for generating downscaled, sector-specific climate information. 4. Low stakeholder knowledge, engagement and awareness: In Mozambique, awareness and engagement levels are low, with limited involvement from local communities and private entities. 5. Limited private sector involvement and financing6. Lack of a holistic and inclusive adaptation approach 7. Inadequate financial resources and budgeting for adaptation: Mozambique’s budget constraints limit its capacity to allocate adequate resources for adaptation.
